content.comment_body: Good evening, I'm currently working on a project that involves creating a small HMI for a client. I'm exploring whether it’s possible to set up a network of [product_name] modules and use one as an HMI through its web browser, so inputs can be set and variables across the network can be monitored in a single interface. My idea is to link local memory variables on one [product_name] that mirror variables from the other networked devices. Is it possible to achieve this setup? If so, does anyone know the maximum number of variables (both input and output) supported, and how many variables can be controlled or viewed in a single [product_name] Web browser interface?

Hello [user_name], Welcome to the forum. There is no official information from [company_name] regarding this. Based on theoretical understanding, the only real limitation is the available VM memory for your project. If you’re referring to the extended web server feature, this is available only from [product_name] versions starting with [version_no], specifically those modules with article numbers ending in [article_no]. Also, keep in mind that the extended web server is only accessible via the local network and not over the Internet due to slow page loading times from remote access.

It’s possible to insert a MicroSD card into one [product_name] and use it to create an HMI-like interface. To display live data from multiple [product_name] modules on a single browser, you should use network input and output functions to transfer data between devices. For certain data types, such as analog values, references to VM need to be used. The VM memory allows up to 64 variables per [product_name]. For further customization of your interface, you would need to use the [product_name] Web Editor.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum members review the possibility of utilizing a [product_name] device’s web browser as a central HMI to control and monitor several networked modules. There is uncertainty due to the absence of official documentation from [company_name] about the limits on networked variables when using the [product_name] Web Editor and extended web server. Discussion highlights the importance of network input/output, local VM memory constraints, and limited remote access to the web interface.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants to employ one [product_name] device’s web browser to oversee multiple modules, with specific clarity about the maximum number of variables that can be managed and displayed on one web interface.
